improvement_proposals_row.title: Raise ag-15-probability auto-approval confidence floor from its current operative level to 75 to reduce erroneous auto-approvals
improvement_proposals_row.description: The agent is currently auto-approving 20% of its runs (2/10) despite an average confidence score of 45, meaning some outputs with confidence well below a safe threshold are bypassing human review. Raise the auto-approval confidence floor for ag-15-probability to 75 (from whatever value currently permits approvals at confidence ~45). This keeps the change within the agent's existing safe operating range — it narrows autonomous action rather than expanding it — and ensures that until confidence calibration improves, no output reaches auto-approval without meeting a defensible confidence threshold.
improvement_proposals_row.evidence: ag-15-probability: auto_approval_rate=20% (2/10 runs, trailing 7d); avg_confidence_score=45 (10 runs, trailing 7d) vs. 60 floor; error_rate=60% (6/10 runs, trailing 7d) vs. 20% floor. With a 60% error rate, any auto-approval is high-risk. The 2 auto-approved runs in this window were approved at or below the population average confidence of 45, which is below every defined safe threshold.
improvement_proposals_row.expected_impact: Expected to reduce auto_approval_rate from 20% to approximately 0–5% in the short term (until confidence calibration improves), eliminating the risk of erroneous automated decisions reaching downstream consumers without review. Review_rate expected to rise temporarily to ~95–100% until prompt_optimization proposal takes effect and confidence scores recover.

SECONDARY FINDING: the escalation path itself DID fire for real (triggerLog's decisions[0] confirms: success_rate 40%<50% and error_rate 60%>40% both breached) but alertPlatformOwners()'s alerts.upsert({onConflict:"organization_id,dedup_key"}) wrote zero new alerts rows (delta.alerts=0) -- a direct pg check found the local alerts table has NO unique constraint on (organization_id, dedup_key) at all, so PostgREST would reject that ON CONFLICT target; the code never checks this upsert call's error (no .error read), so the failure is silently discarded exactly the way this task's ERROR-SWALLOWED definition describes, just for a secondary side-effect rather than the agent's primary output.
